To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
soil landscape and ecosystem properties can be predicted from terrain variables.

soil landscape patterns are the result of the integration of short- and long-term pedogeomorphic processes that can be modeled using terrain attributes and that the resulting models are useful for testing hypotheses about landscape and ecosystem properties and for parameterizing distributed hydrological and biogeochemical models.

(1) the spatial distribution of soil landscape properties can be modeled from easily measured terrain attributes; (2) these models are explicit and can be used to test hypotheses about the spatial variation of fine scale landscape processes; and (3) the models are quantitative and can be used for spatially distributed hydrologic and ecosystem simulation models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a spatially explicit, quantitative framework for understanding the spatial variability of soil landscape and ecosystem properties and processes.
the development of quantitative, spatially distributed models of soil landscape and ecosystem properties that will allow for more realistic simulation of soil landscape and hydrologic processes.
the spatial distribution of soil properties and their implications for ecosystem processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soil surveyors should use terrain attributes as a basis for mapping soil landscapes.
the models developed in this study are useful tools for the prediction of spatial patterns of soil properties, and that they can be applied to other landscapes and soil properties.
soil landscape and ecosystem properties are predictable from digital terrain attributes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new quantitative approach to soil landscape analysis that is applicable to a wide range of soil landscape and ecosystem processes.

soil landscape patterns result from complex interactions between pedogenesis and geomorphic processes and are best modeled using a combination of field and remote sensing data and quantitative spatial analysis techniques.

the spatial variability in soil properties can be explained by the spatial distribution of topographic variables and that the spatial variability is a result of differential soil formation processes in landscape positions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil landscape and ecosystem patterns are predictable from easily measured terrain attributes.
soil properties are strongly related to landscape position and that this relationship can be modeled using terrain attributes.
soil landscape models are useful tools for understanding and managing soil and landscape patterns and processes.
